title: Add Dedicated staged-rollout traffic shift canary scenario (reserved pool)
author: Leila Farouk
description:
Context: Dedicated staged rollouts introduce deterministic stage weights + gate evaluation. We’ve already seen a few classes of regressions during dogfood (routing hash drift, allocator churn, and evaluator lag causing traffic shifts to happen too quickly). This PR adds a perf-canary scenario that simulates staged rollout traffic shifts on a reserved pool so we can detect regressions before enabling features for additional tenants.

What this adds: (1) New scenario `dedicated_staged_rollout_shift` that runs a steady-state workload (mixed prompt lengths + streaming) and then performs 3 traffic-shift steps (5% -> 25% -> 100%) while keeping total QPS constant. (2) Assertions around p50/p95 latency deltas, queue depth, timeout/5xx rate, and (optionally) GPU utilization when the signal is available. (3) A "metrics freshness" preflight check to avoid false positives when the metrics pipeline is lagging; if freshness fails, the scenario marks the run as "infra" failure (non-regression) and alerts #eng-sre for investigation.

Implementation notes: Traffic shift is driven by the rollout control plane API (approve + advance stage) using a test tenant/pool allowlisted for canaries. The scenario reads the stage status and blocks until routing confirms the new allocation epoch (we key off the stage change event id to avoid racing). To keep cardinality low, scenario metrics are tagged only by {scenario, pool_id, step} and we sample per-request spans.

Success criteria / thresholds (defaults): p95 latency increase <= 12% after each step (relative to pre-shift baseline), queue depth p95 <= 2x baseline for > 3 minutes triggers fail, timeout_rate <= 0.3%, 5xx_rate <= 0.2%. These match the initial Dedicated rollout gating defaults being proposed, but are slightly looser to avoid flaking until evaluator + routing settle.

Rollout / ops: The scenario is behind feature flag `CANARY_DEDICATED_STAGED_ROLLOUT_SHIFT` and only runs in nightly + release candidate pipelines. It does not run on PRs by default because it requires reserved pool access.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): add an optional "missing-metrics" simulation step (force the evaluator into hold) once the staging harness supports toggling evaluator health; add a variant that uses two model versions to capture KV-cache and compile-time impacts.

Refs: ENG-5132, ENG-5123, ENG-5124. Related: redwood#28572 (fail-safe hold when evaluator degraded).
commits: scenario: add dedicated staged rollout traffic-shift scenario skeleton
scenario: implement step runner and stage advancement via rollout API
assertions: baseline capture + per-step regression checks (latency/errors/queue depth)
metrics: add freshness preflight and classify infra failures
config: wire scenario into nightly/rc pipelines behind flag
docs: update scenario catalog + oncall note
conversation: Mina Haddad (review): The stage advancement block looks good, but can we guarantee we’re not racing on routing propagation? Right now it waits for control plane state only.

Leila Farouk (author): Good catch. I added a second barrier: we poll the routing epoch exposed by the canary-side router probe and require it to match the stage event id before starting the next measurement window. See latest push in `runner.ts`.
Logan Wright (review): Please keep metric labels low-cardinality. `tenant_name` shouldn’t be a label in any of these queries.

Leila Farouk (author): Removed `tenant_name` and switched to `pool_id` only; also collapsed `step_name` into a small enum (`baseline`, `s1_5`, `s2_25`, `s3_100`). Added a comment in `assertions.ts` about cardinality constraints.
Thomas Baird (review): The p95 delta threshold at 8% seems optimistic given current variability. We’ll end up flaking during RC.
Leila Farouk (author): Agreed. Set default to 12% and require a sustained breach over 3 minutes before failing. We still alert on single-window spikes but don’t fail the run.
Sean Gallagher (review): For freshness preflight, can we route the failure to SRE without paging product folks? Also ensure it’s clearly "infra" in the summary.
Leila Farouk (author): Updated classification: `INFRA_METRICS_STALE` with dedicated notification to #eng-sre only; the PR summary output now calls it out explicitly.
Mina Haddad (approval): Approved. This should catch the hash drift class of bugs we saw in staging.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved with the label changes. Thanks for keeping the tags clean.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Please link in the SRE runbook follow-up once merged.
Thomas Baird (approval): Approved after threshold adjustments.
release_notes: Internal: Added a perf-canary scenario that simulates Dedicated staged rollout traffic shifts (5%/25%/100%) on a reserved pool and fails on sustained latency/error/queue depth regressions; includes metrics freshness preflight to avoid false positives.
